parameters.query:
SELECT
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_cancellations WHERE order_id = $1) AS cancelled,
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM orders this_order
    JOIN orders later ON later.customer_id = this_order.customer_id AND later.received_at > this_order.received_at
    WHERE this_order.order_id = $1
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_cancellations c WHERE c.order_id = later.order_id)
  ) AS reordered,
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE order_id = $1) AS recorded;

nodes.name: Build reorder reminder
nodes.notes: Why Code: decides consent, cancellation, and reorder in one tested place and renders the branded reminder with a cart link in the customer's language

parameters.content:
## Wait, then re-check
Started by Process order only when the customer accepted marketing at checkout. Waits reorder_reminder_days, then reads the order's status again: a cancelled order, or one the same customer has since followed with another uncancelled order, gets nothing.

## Build and send
Build reorder reminder decides again from the order's consent and email, and renders the branded email with a cart link for the same bags. Only a reminder marked send reaches Gmail.
NOTE: one waiting execution per consenting order lives in Postgres for reorder_reminder_days. Ceiling: a small store's volume. Upgrade path: a daily scheduled query for orders due a reminder.
